original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Does low_weight_words at its default batch size 16, on the reflected 36-generator basis of PR #7017, return the seven transported supports with hash 9ce7e5edc72ee3104d62cb068146b73840e9a3c42c4132403dece70c8146cccb?
scope_change_reason: The replay-runtime card asks for a measured speedup. The revision-8 verification row says a published faster replay is equivalent coverage only after the sets are compared. Open PR #7017 recorded the reflected P112 half-split and asked whether low_weight_words on that 36-generator basis returns the transported supports. This package answers that set comparison at the function's default batch size. It does not time an engine or rerun the half-split.
bottleneck_link: Frame-code coverage checks remain usable only when the published bit-lane iterator returns the same low-weight set as the recorded supports. This comparison binds that iterator to the reflected P112 basis. It does not change a supplier bill or the selected kappa.
stop_rule: Stop after one call of low_weight_words at batch size 16 on this ordered reflected basis, compared with the transported support hash. Do not run another batch size, reverse the basis, rerun the half-split, or call the intersection-counter engine.
evidence: The reflected basis rebuilt from the pinned E8 line list and simple system matches the #7017 free coordinates, basis weights, line-list hash a2ac7049d9eef1cff8af1eec35b084e6d261efad5311625e5356cceafe260da7, and transported-support hash 9ce7e5edc72ee3104d62cb068146b73840e9a3c42c4132403dece70c8146cccb. The 36 generators have hash f71157e487ad45377cb6a92651d3a8d8b1055b6978f14a44dea511049ca7da8c. low_weight_words at batch size 16 returns exactly zero and those seven weight-16 supports, with no repeated yield. A dropped support, a weight-15 injection, the untransported integers, a repeated generator, and a toy bound change all fail. Selected kappa stays 781451/250000000.
author: unpaidmoon

open_questions.question: Does low_weight_words at batch size 20 on this same ordered reflected basis return the same seven transported supports?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Batch size 20 is the size used for the unreflected basis in #7007. The iterator says batch size changes storage and runtime only. This package executes the default batch size 16, so that claim is unchecked at batch 20 on this basis.
open_questions.first_step: Call low_weight_words at batch size 20 on the generator tuple with hash f71157e487ad45377cb6a92651d3a8d8b1055b6978f14a44dea511049ca7da8c and compare the positive words with hash 9ce7e5edc72ee3104d62cb068146b73840e9a3c42c4132403dece70c8146cccb.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package stops after the batch-16 call. A second scan is a separate execution.

open_questions.question: Does the reversed 36-tuple, at batch size 16, return the same set?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The iterator's result is claimed independent of generator order once the rows stay independent. This package uses the free-coordinate order only.
open_questions.first_step: Reverse the pinned generator tuple and repeat the batch-16 call against the same transported hash.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package does not reverse the basis.
